Hi Amelia — Monica from Redwood security here. Thanks for sending the questionnaire (I see it in the thread). I pulled together high-level answers to the items you flagged during the call — see below. I can annotate the spreadsheet once we get a clean copy; for now, these answers should help you triage internally.

1) SOC 2 status
- Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; most customers are covered under our hosted offering. We can share the SOC 2 report under NDA and coordinate any redaction needs.

2) GDPR / Data residency
- We support EU regions and offer data residency controls for customer data. DPA is standard; we can provide our template and accept reasonable amendments.

3) HIPAA / PHI handling
- We support HIPAA workflows via Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated reservations with customer contracts & BAAs in place. For your PHI workloads, we recommend Private deployment or dedicated tenancy to reduce blast radius.

4) Encryption at-rest and in-transit
- At-rest: AES-256 envelope encryption. Keys are stored in a KMS-backed model; for hosted customers we use cloud KMSs (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) in isolated key accounts per customer.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 by default) with forward secrecy.

5) KMS / HSM / BYOK support
- BYOK / CMK: Supported. Customers can bring keys to AWS KMS and use customer-managed CMKs for envelope encryption with our hosted and dedicated offerings.
- HSM-backed keys: We support HSM-backed keys via cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM) and can integrate with customer HSMs for Private deployments.
- Key material access: Redwood does not have access to plaintext CMKs when BYOK is used — we only receive wrapped keys or use KMS-based encryption APIs. We can provide an architecture diagram and sequence showing that plaintext keys never leave the customer-managed KMS/HSM.

6) Key rotation and lifecycle
- Rotation: We support KMS-driven rotation policies; customers control rotation schedules. For BYOK, rotation must be coordinated as part of onboarding; we document required re-wrapping steps.

7) Auditability / logs
- Key usage and cryptographic operations are logged and can be included in audit packages. Access to key operations is logged in both our control plane and customer KMS audit trails.

Next steps I propose:
- Please send the vendor questionnaire as an editable spreadsheet (attached by Amelia). We'll annotate the sheet and return within 3 business days.
- Schedule a 30-minute technical Q&A with me and Jonas to walk through the CMK architecture diagram and confirm the BYOK onboarding flow.

Attachments I will add to the annotated response: redwood-security-brief.pdf (concise answers and references), cmk-arch-diagram.pdf (sequence & boundary diagram).

If there are specific QSA questions that need deeper evidence (key escrow policies, HSM attestation), flag them in the sheet and I will gather the artifacts required.

Regards,

Great questions, Amelia — short answers here and then next-step logistics:

- On-prem HSM key import: Supported for Private deployments. For hosted/Dedicated we support importing keys into a cloud KMS (AWS KMS) via secure wrapping; a direct HSM-to-HSM transfer is possible when customers run a Private deployment and provide a validated connection to their HSM appliance. Monica will detail the import checklist.
- Plaintext key access: No — Redwood does not have access to plaintext customer-managed key material when BYOK/CMK is used. Keys remain under customer control in their KMS/HSM. We can provide a one-page attestation for your QSA if helpful.
- Onboarding timeline: Private deployment + HSM integration typically takes 4–8 weeks depending on networking and attestation requirements; Dedicated + KMS BYOK import can be completed in ~2–3 weeks in most cases. Exact timelines depend on your security review and calendar.
